title: Lab Report Digitisation and Trend Extraction
summary: Turn external lab reports, PDFs and phone photos into structured results mapped to standard test codes, and show trends over time to the treating doctor with every value linked to its source.

seo.title: Lab Report Digitisation and Trends with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Digitise lab reports from any lab, map tests to LOINC, normalise units safely and show result trends to doctors, with each value linked to its report.

designed_for: Consultant physicians in chronic care clinics

problem.intro: Patients with diabetes, kidney disease or thyroid conditions arrive with a folder of reports from different labs, or a phone full of PDFs and photos. The doctor flips through pages to find last year's HbA1c or creatinine, while test names, units and reference ranges differ from lab to lab.

pain_points.title: Different names for the same test
pain_points.detail: Glycated haemoglobin, HbA1c and A1c appear on different reports, and each lab lays out its panels differently.

pain_points.title: Unit and range differences
pain_points.detail: Results arrive in mg/dL, mmol/L or micromol/L with lab-specific reference ranges, which makes side-by-side comparison error-prone.

pain_points.title: Consultation time spent searching
pain_points.detail: Minutes of a short OPD slot go on locating prior values instead of talking to the patient.

pain_points.title: Reports outside the HIS
pain_points.detail: External reports are scanned as images, if at all, so they never appear in trend views or registries.

solution.overview: We build a lab report digitisation service that reads reports from any lab, whether native PDFs, scans or phone photos. It extracts each test name, result, unit, reference range as printed, sample date and lab name, and maps tests to a standard code system such as LOINC so that equivalent tests line up. Units are converted only where the conversion is on a list your laboratory medicine team approves, and the original value is always kept. Results flow into the patient record and a trend view that shows values over time, with each point linked to its source report. Values outside the printed reference range are marked as such; interpretation stays with the doctor.
capabilities: Reads native PDFs, scans and phone photos from any lab, including multi-page panels
Extracts test name, result, unit, printed reference range, sample date and lab
Maps tests to a standard code system such as LOINC, with a review queue for unmapped names
Converts units only from an approved list and always keeps the original value
Builds trend views for chronic-care markers your clinicians choose, with source links on every point
Detects duplicate uploads of the same report

workflow.title: Receive reports
workflow.detail: Reports arrive through front-desk scanning, patient upload on WhatsApp or an app, or lab interfaces.

workflow.title: Extract results
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM extract each test, result, unit, range and date, with a confidence score for each.

workflow.title: Map and normalise
workflow.detail: Tests are mapped to standard codes and units normalised where approved; unmapped or low-confidence items are queued.

workflow.title: Review exceptions
workflow.detail: A trained data reviewer or nurse confirms flagged items against the source image.

workflow.title: Update the record
workflow.detail: Confirmed results are written to the patient record and appear in the trend view.

workflow.title: Doctor views trends
workflow.detail: During the consultation, the doctor sees trends with links to the source reports and interprets them.

inputs: External lab reports as PDFs, scans or phone photos
Patient identifiers from the HIS, such as UHID
Test name mapping list maintained by the lab or informatics team
Unit conversion list approved by laboratory medicine
outputs: Structured results with test code, value, unit, range and date
Exception queue for unmapped or uncertain results
Audit trail of extraction and reviewer changes
human_in_the_loop: A trained reviewer confirms any uncertain or unmapped result before it enters the record, and the laboratory medicine team approves the unit conversion list. Doctors interpret every result; the system only organises and displays them.
integrations: HIS or EMR (HL7, FHIR or API)
Laboratory information system for in-house results
WhatsApp Business API or patient app for uploads
ABDM-linked health record apps where the patient consents
guardrails: Original value and unit always stored alongside any converted value
Conversions only from the approved list; all others shown as printed
No interpretive comments, risk scores or diagnoses generated
Patient matching on UHID with name and age checks to prevent misfiling
Every trend point links back to its source page
compliance_notes: Patient-uploaded reports handled with consent and purpose limitation under the DPDP Act 2023.
Structured outputs can follow FHIR-based formats used in ABDM where the hospital is integrated.

pilot.scope: External reports for patients of one chronic-care clinic, such as diabetes or nephrology, digitised for a set of common markers.
deliverables: Test mapping and unit conversion lists for the pilot markers
Accuracy report per test and report format

what_we_measure.how: Extracted results compared with manually entered values for a sample of reports.
Test names mapped automatically compared with those sent for review.
Reports linked to the wrong patient, found through reviewer checks.
Structured feedback from pilot doctors on whether the trend view helped them find prior results.

faqs.q: Does it interpret results or flag diseases?
faqs.a: No. It shows values, units, the lab's printed reference range and trends. Whether a value matters for the patient is the doctor's call.

faqs.q: How do you handle method differences between labs?
faqs.a: Every result is shown with its lab name and printed range, so the doctor can see the source. Unit conversions are limited to a list approved by your laboratory medicine team.
Yes, through WhatsApp or your app, with consent captured at upload. Each report is matched to the patient record and checked before it enters the trend view.
Any test printed on a report can be extracted. Trend views start with markers your clinicians choose, such as HbA1c, creatinine, lipid profile and TSH, and expand from there.
